A · The tool, as it opens
on this Mac, with the notebook’s own two photos

svg.text: Left: the dataset. Right: one photo.

text.tspan: Each photo in the tree shows its size, how many people it has and its mark — train or test; a click on the mark
switches it. The open photo lists its people back to front, each in their own colour. Clicking a person, in the list or
on the canvas, selects them: their corner points appear. The buttons act on what is selected and grey out when
there is nothing to act on; the line under the canvas counts people and points and says when there is something
zoomed in on one shoulder: a new point (white) pulled out of its edge by the square handle

svg.text: Zoom in, then move and add points.

text.tspan: The mouse wheel zooms around the pointer, + and − around the middle, Fit shows the whole photo; dragging an
empty spot moves the photo around. A selected person shows round points and, in the middle of every edge, a
small square. Drag a round point to move it. Drag a square to pull a new point out of that edge — here one is
being pulled out at the shoulder, and its two new edges get squares of their own; a click on a square adds the
point right there. Zoomed in, shorter edges get squares too, so points go exactly where the outline needs them.
More points adds one to every edge of the person at once. Pick a point and press Delete to remove it; Ctrl or
zoomed in: the wall between her arm and her side, dashed, left out of her fill

svg.text: Inside the outline, but not the person.

text.tspan: An outline follows a person’s edge, so where an arm makes a loop — a hand on the hip, a hand at the glasses
— the wall seen through the loop ends up inside it. Add hole cuts it out: select the person, click Add hole and
click around the gap, then double-click or press Enter. A hole is drawn dashed and is not filled, and in the mask
it shows whatever is behind it — the wall, or a person further back. Its points move, multiply and go like any
others; deleting a hole’s points down to two removes it. In the labels,

tspan.style: font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace;font-size:11.8px;font-weight:600;fill:var(--ink)

text.tspan: , the rest drawn in this tool.
New person, then click by click around the outline

svg.text: Click the corner points, then close.

text.tspan: New person starts an outline: every click adds a corner point and a dashed line follows the mouse. A
double-click or Enter closes it, Esc throws it away. The new person gets the next free number and goes to the
front; Move behind and Move in front change their place, which decides who keeps the pixels where two outlines
overlap. Add part draws a second outline for the selected person — a hand showing on the far side of someone
else. (Here the points were placed around a person who already has an outline, to show the drawing.)
